finding: The installed app was running and had created its status item; iBar Pro's live menu-bar cache omitted it until iBar Pro was restarted and Disk Steward was relaunched.
disconfirmed_hypotheses: The installed app was rejected by Gatekeeper.
The installed app crashed during launch.
The app failed to create an NSStatusItem.
Automatic termination was required to explain the missing icon.

checks.evidence: valid on disk; satisfies its Designated Requirement
status=launched, activation_policy=accessory, status_item_accessibility_label=Disk Steward, left and right click surfaces present

checks.command: pgrep and launchctl inspection before recovery
checks.evidence: PID 63908 and application.com.marudankiji.disksteward were live while the icon was absent
arrOfAlwaysDisplay contained Item-0 >>> com.marudankiji.disksteward, proving the persisted rule and live presentation were inconsistent

checks.command: restart iBar Pro; open -n '/Applications/Disk Steward.app'; capture menu bar
checks.evidence: PID 74859 remained registered and the Disk Steward drive icon was visibly restored immediately to the right of iBar's ellipsis control

checks.command: xcodebuild -project DiskSteward.xcodeproj -scheme DiskSteward -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath /private/tmp/disk-steward-task210-derived CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

recovery: Quit and reopen iBar Pro to refresh its menu-bar item cache.
Confirm the drive icon appears immediately to the right of iBar's ellipsis control.
limitations: A third-party menu-bar manager can hide or temporarily omit any status item independently of the app's process lifecycle.
Disk Steward cannot force another application's live item cache to refresh.
